name: wm97xx_init_pen_irq
prose: Precondition: wm points to an initialized wm97xx whose pen_irq holds an IRQ number the caller wants for pen-down interrupts (IRQF_SHARED is used, so other users may share the line); if wm->id is not WM9705_ID2 then wm->mach_ops must be non-NULL (it is dereferenced before the BUG_ON test) and wm->mach_ops->irq_gpio must be nonzero (BUG_ON(!irq_gpio) fires otherwise). Postcondition: if request_threaded_irq(wm->pen_irq, NULL, wm97xx_pen_interrupt, IRQF_SHARED | IRQF_ONESHOT, "wm97xx-pen", wm) fails, it logs an error, sets wm->pen_irq to 0, performs no codec register access and returns -EINVAL. Otherwise, for wm->id != WM9705_ID2 it reads AC97_MISC_AFE and writes it back with the irq_gpio bits cleared, then reads register 0x5a and writes it back with only bit 0x0001 cleared; for WM9705 no register is accessed; in both cases it returns 0 with the threaded handler left registered.
note: reviewer R15 (NULL mach_ops dereferences before BUG_ON) is right: wm->mach_ops->irq_gpio is read in the BUG_ON in the BUG_ON so NULL mach_ops oopses instead of reaching BUG_ON; R2 (only bit 0x0001 of 0x5a, shared IRQ) right; original rejection (WM9705 configures no GPIO; BUG_ON needs irq_gpio) right. All incorporated.

name: add_early_maps
prose: Precondition: the early_ioapic_map, early_hpet_map and early_acpihid_map arrays hold early_ioapic_map_size, early_hpet_map_size and early_acpihid_map_size valid entries (cmd_line, id/devid, and NUL-terminated hid/uid for the ACPI HID entries); runs at init (__init). Postcondition: walks the IOAPIC entries, then the HPET entries (add_special_device), then the ACPI HID entries (add_acpi_hid_device), and returns the first nonzero value any of those calls returns without processing later entries, or 0 if all succeed. The callees return -ENOMEM when their kzalloc fails (earlier registrations stay in the lists), add_special_device also returns -EINVAL for a type other than IOAPIC or HPET (not reachable from the types passed here); when an existing command-line entry matches, the callee returns 0 without allocating and overwrites the early map entry's devid with that entry's devid.
note: contract dropped: function reads/writes global early maps and lists; prior prose said only -ENOMEM which omits propagated callee codes. Source lines 1423-1450.

name: qcom_tbu_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device whose device node may carry the "qcom,stream-id-range" property (two cells after #iommu-cells), an iomem resource 0, an optional clock and an interconnect path; the caller holds nothing relevant. Postcondition: allocates a device-managed qcom_tbu (devm_kzalloc) and initializes its list head and halt_lock. Returns -ENOMEM if the allocation fails; -EINVAL (after dev_err) if of_parse_phandle_with_args on "qcom,stream-id-range" fails; otherwise it records smmu_np and the two stream-id range values, drops the reference taken on args.np with of_node_put (smmu_np keeps the pointer), and then returns PTR_ERR of the first failing devm_of_iomap, devm_clk_get_optional or devm_of_icc_get result. On success it takes tbu_list_lock (scope-based guard), appends the tbu to the global tbu_list, releases the lock when the function returns, and returns 0. On every error path the tbu is not on tbu_list; devm-managed resources are released by the driver core, not by this function.
note: slice cut the head: packet name tbu_probe_tail is invented, real function is qcom_tbu_probe (file lines 476-517), slice 505-517 is its tail. Described the whole function.

name: get_stash_id
prose: Precondition: stash_dest_hint is a PAMU_ATTR_CACHE_L1/L2/L3 value (1, 2, 3) or any other u32, vcpu is a CPU number compared with the "reg" values of device-tree CPU nodes. Postcondition: returns the cache-stash-id value or ~(u32)0 on failure. If stash_dest_hint == PAMU_ATTR_CACHE_L3 it finds the first node matching l3_device_ids and returns its "cache-stash-id" (be32_to_cpup of the property), or ~(u32)0 if no node matches or the property is missing (the node reference is dropped with of_node_put in both cases). Otherwise it scans the CPU nodes for one whose "reg" contains vcpu; if none is found it returns ~(u32)0 with no reference held. If found, it walks up to cache levels L1 and L2: at the level equal to stash_dest_hint it returns that node's "cache-stash-id" (or ~(u32)0 if missing), dropping the node reference first; at lower levels it follows "next-level-cache" (using of_find_node_by_phandle on the raw property word) and returns ~(u32)0 if that property is missing (node reference dropped) or the phandle does not resolve. If stash_dest_hint is not 1 or 2 (and not 3), the walk ends after L2 and the function returns ~(u32)0 without releasing the last node reference it obtained, so that reference is leaked.
note: reviewer R15 right: after the for loop the last node from of_find_node_by_phandle is never put when stash_dest_hint is outside L1/L2, contradicting 'every reference released'. R1 (contract) moot. Contract left empty.

name: iommufd_hwpt_invalidate
prose: Precondition: ucmd->cmd points to a struct iommu_hwpt_invalidate from userspace, and ucmd->ictx is a valid iommufd context. Postcondition: if cmd->__reserved is nonzero, rc = -EOPNOTSUPP; else if cmd->entry_num is nonzero and any of data_uptr == 0, entry_len == 0, entry_len > PAGE_SIZE or entry_num > IOMMU_HWPT_INVALIDATE_ENTRY_NUM_MAX holds, rc = -EINVAL; both without looking up an object. Otherwise it looks up cmd->hwpt_id with iommufd_get_object (any type); on lookup error rc = PTR_ERR. If the object is a nested HWPT it calls the domain's cache_invalidate_user op (rc = -EOPNOTSUPP if ops or the op is NULL); if a vIOMMU it calls viommu->ops->cache_invalidate (-EOPNOTSUPP if missing); any other type gives -EINVAL. After a backend call (whatever its result) done_num = data_array.entry_num; the object reference is dropped with iommufd_put_object on all paths after a successful lookup. Finally cmd->entry_num = done_num (0 if no backend ran) and the command is copied back with iommufd_ucmd_respond; if that fails it returns -EFAULT, overriding rc; otherwise it returns rc (0 on success, or one of the errors above or the backend's error).
note: slice cut the head: packet name iommufd_cache_invalidate_ucmd_handler (excerpt) is not a real function; real enclosing function is iommufd_hwpt_invalidate (file lines 495-563). Old prose 'bad combination' ok but missed that entry_num is reported even on backend error.

name: mpic_ipi_init
prose: Precondition: built with CONFIG_SMP; mpic and node are valid. Postcondition: sets mpic->ipi_domain to the result of irq_domain_create_linear(of_fwnode_handle(node), IPI_DOORBELL_NR, ...); if that is NULL it issues a WARN and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise it sets the domain's bus token to DOMAIN_BUS_IPI and calls irq_domain_alloc_irqs(ipi_domain, IPI_DOORBELL_NR, NUMA_NO_NODE, NULL), storing the result in base_ipi. Only the value 0 is treated as failure (WARN and return -ENOMEM, with mpic->ipi_domain left set and not freed); any other value, including a negative error code from irq_domain_alloc_irqs, is passed to set_smp_ipi_range(base_ipi, IPI_DOORBELL_NR) and the function returns 0.
note: reviewers R1/R2/R15 right: irq-armada-370-xp.c:315 only checks !base_ipi, negative errors are not detected and not returned. Old prose said 'positive base' and omitted that. Function is inside #ifdef CONFIG_SMP.

name: free_lpi_range
prose: Precondition: nr_lpis > 0 (not checked) and [base, base + nr_lpis) is not already present in lpi_range_list. Postcondition: it allocates a list node with kmalloc(GFP_KERNEL) via mk_lpi_range before taking any lock; if that fails it returns -ENOMEM with the list unchanged and lpi_range_lock not taken. Otherwise it takes lpi_range_lock (mutex), scans the list from the tail for the last range with base_id < base, inserts the new node right after it (at the head of the list if none), then merges the preceding range into the new node when the preceding range ends exactly at base, and merges the new node into the following range when it ends exactly at that range's base_id (the absorbed node is removed and kfree'd, so the surviving node may be the neighbour rather than the new node), releases the mutex and returns 0.
note: prior prose nearly right; added that merge frees one of the nodes. Source irq-gic-v3-its.c:2149-2161. Contract removed (globals, mutex).

name: allocate_vpe_l1_table
prose: Precondition: called on the CPU whose redistributor is being set up, with gic_rdists initialized; vlpi_base is obtained from gic_data_rdist_vlpi_base() at entry. Postcondition: if gic_rdists->has_rvpeid is false it returns 0 without touching any register. Otherwise, if GICR_VPENDBASER has Valid set, it writes GICR_VPENDBASER_PendingLast (Valid clear). It then tries inherit_vpe_l1_table_from_rd: if that yields a VPROPBASER value with the 4.1 Valid bit, vpe_table_mask and vpe_l1_base now refer to the donor CPU's mask and L1 table (no new allocation) and the function jumps to the common exit. If not, it kzallocs a cpumask (GFP_ATOMIC) into this redistributor's vpe_table_mask, returning -ENOMEM if that fails (no VPROPBASER write after the optional pending-VPE write). It then tries inherit_vpe_l1_table_from_its; if that value is Valid it goes to the common exit. Otherwise it probes the page size by writing a 64K page-size value to GICR_VPROPBASER, derives psz/entry size/number of L1 pages, allocates the zeroed L1 table with its_alloc_pages (GFP_ATOMIC|__GFP_ZERO), and returns -ENOMEM if that fails (leaving the new, empty mask installed, vpe_l1_base unset, VPROPBASER holding the probe value, and this CPU not set in the mask). On success it records vpe_l1_base, builds the VPROPBASER value (address, size, optional indirect/shareability bits, Z and Valid). At the common exit it writes that value to GICR_VPROPBASER, sets the current CPU in vpe_table_mask and returns 0.
note: prior prose lumped 'inherit from RD' with allocated mask; corrected: RD-inherit reuses the donor's mask pointer. Source irq-gic-v3-its.c:2899-2993 (file lines). Contract removed (globals, hardware).

name: gic_acpi_collect_gicr_base
prose: Precondition: runs at init (__init) after the ACPI MADT is available; acpi_data.single_redist selects the parser. Postcondition: if acpi_data.single_redist is set it parses MADT GENERIC_INTERRUPT (GICC) entries with gic_acpi_parse_madt_gicc, otherwise GENERIC_REDISTRIBUTOR entries with gic_acpi_parse_madt_redist, via acpi_table_parse_madt. If that call returns a value greater than 0 it returns 0. Otherwise (zero or negative) it prints "No valid GICR entries exist" and returns -ENODEV (-19). The parsers may record redistributor regions in acpi_data as a side effect.
note: reviewer R15 about contract only; prose kept but tightened ('at least one entry parsed' replaced by 'acpi_table_parse_madt returns >0'). Source irq-gic-v3.c:2470-2487. Contract removed (globals).

name: irq_matrix_init
prose: Precondition: called during init (__init). Postcondition: it stores irq_alloc_matrix(NR_VECTORS, 0, NR_VECTORS) in loongarch_avec.vector_matrix; if that is NULL it returns -ENOMEM with vector_matrix NULL and nothing else done. Otherwise it calls irq_matrix_assign_system(vector_matrix, i, false) for i = 0 .. NR_LEGACY_VECTORS-1, calls irq_matrix_online(vector_matrix) and returns 0.
note: prior prose correct; contract removed (touches global loongarch_avec). Source irq-loongarch-avec.c:336-348.

name: release_io_hfcmulti
prose: Precondition: hc is a struct hfc_multi whose registers are accessible (the soft reset writes R_CIRM through HFC_outb) and whose pci_membase/plx_membase/pci_iobase/xhfc_membase/pci_dev fields are either zero/NULL or valid mappings the driver owns. Postcondition: returns void. It sets V_SRES in hc->hw.r_cirm, writes R_CIRM, waits 1 ms, clears V_SRES, writes again and waits 1 ms. If HFC_CHIP_PLXSD is set and plx_membase is non-NULL it takes plx_lock with interrupts saved, writes PLX_GPIOC_INIT then rewrites PLX_GPIOC with termination off, PCM disconnected (slave enable set, master and sync-out enable cleared) and the DSP held in reset, and releases plx_lock. It then clears HFC_CHIP_PLXSD, writes 0 to PCI_COMMAND if hc->pci_dev is set, calls iounmap on pci_membase, plx_membase and (if non-zero) xhfc_membase, release_region(pci_iobase, 8) if pci_iobase is nonzero, and, if pci_dev is set, pci_disable_device and pci_set_drvdata(pci_dev, NULL). The hc pointer fields themselves are not cleared.
note: slice cut the head: packet name '(unnamed card teardown, ...)' is not a function name; real function is release_io_hfcmulti (file lines 1006-1070, slice 1051-1307 starts inside it). Fixed under real name.

name: mode_hfcmulti
prose: Precondition: hc points to an initialized hfc_multi whose chan[] (indexable 0..31) and slot_owner[] arrays are valid for the slot numbers used, and the caller serializes hardware access (the function takes no lock). Postcondition: if ch < 0 or ch > 31 it returns -EINVAL before reading or writing anything. Otherwise: (1) if the channel's stored TX slot is >= 0 and differs from slot_tx, and slot_owner[old_tx << 1] == ch, it writes R_SLOT and A_SL_CFG = 0 (and A_CONF = 0 unless ctype is HFC_TYPE_XHFC) and sets that owner to -1; the same for the stored RX slot against slot_rx (owner slot_owner[(old_rx << 1) | 1], no A_CONF write); if another channel owns the slot nothing is written. (2) For slot_tx < 0 it stores slot_tx = -1, bank_tx = 0 in chan[ch] without writing slot registers; otherwise it programs R_SLOT/A_SL_CFG (and A_CONF unless XHFC), sets slot_owner[slot_tx << 1] = ch and stores slot_tx/bank_tx; likewise for RX (slot_owner[(slot_rx << 1) | 1], no A_CONF). (3) It then switches on protocol: ISDN_P_NONE disables both FIFOs and, if chan[ch].bch is set, clears FLG_HDLC and FLG_TRANSPARENT in bch->Flags, and (also only if bch is set and ctype != HFC_TYPE_E1) clears the B1/B2 enable bit in hw.a_st_ctrl0 for the port and writes A_ST_CTRL0; ISDN_P_B_RAW sets the FIFOs up for transparent HDLC (a pass-through setup with vpm_out when HFC_CHIP_B410P is set and both stored slots are negative), issues FIFO resets only when the stored protocol differs from protocol, sets the B1/B2 enable bit and writes A_ST_CTRL0 when ctype != HFC_TYPE_E1, and sets FLG_TRANSPARENT if bch is non-NULL; ISDN_P_B_HDLC, ISDN_P_TE_S0, ISDN_P_NT_S0, ISDN_P_TE_E1 and ISDN_P_NT_E1 enable both FIFOs for HDLC with interrupts and, only if bch is non-NULL, set FLG_HDLC and (for ctype != E1) set the B-channel enable bit and write A_ST_CTRL0. For these protocols it stores protocol in chan[ch].protocol and returns 0. For any other protocol it prints a debug message, sets chan[ch].protocol = ISDN_P_NONE and returns -ENOPROTOOPT, after the slot release and slot/bank updates of steps (1)-(2) have already been done.
note: line refs hfcmulti.c mode_hfcmulti file lines 2818-3139. Old prose said 'enabling the S/T line transceiver' (really the B1/B2 enable bit in A_ST_CTRL0, only for non-E1) and set HDLC flags unconditionally (only if bch). Contract removed (hc state, hardware).

prose: Precondition: hc points to an initialized hfc_multi whose chan[] (indexable 0..31) and slot_owner[] arrays are valid for the slot numbers used, and the caller serializes hardware access (the function takes no lock). name: dsp_cmx_hardware
prose: Precondition: either conf is non-NULL and its mlist holds struct dsp_conf_member entries with valid ->dsp, or conf is NULL and dsp is non-NULL; the caller serializes access to dsp_ilist, the dsp structures and the conference (this function takes no lock, allocates nothing, returns void). Postcondition: if conf and dsp are both NULL it returns doing nothing. Single-dsp update (conf NULL, or a conference with exactly one member, for which it first sets conf->hardware = 0 and conf->software = 0): if dsp->hfc_conf >= 0 it sends MISDN_CTRL_HFC_CONF_SPLIT and sets hfc_conf = -1; if features.pcm_banks < 1 it returns; if neither echo.software nor echo.hardware is set it, when a TX or RX PCM slot is assigned, sends MISDN_CTRL_HFC_PCM_DISC and sets both slots and banks to -1, then returns; with echo enabled it sets echo.software = tx_data and echo.hardware = 0, keeps an existing loop assignment (tx slot >= 0, rx slot < 0, both banks 2) as hardware echo, or reuses an assigned tx slot for rx with banks 2 (sending MISDN_CTRL_HFC_PCM_CONN), or picks the first free PCM slot (among dsps of the same pcm_id) and assigns it to tx and rx with banks 2 and sends PCM_CONN; each of those sets echo.hardware = 1; if no slot below features.pcm_slots is free it sets echo.software = 1 and leaves the slots at -1. Conference update (conf non-NULL): an empty mlist prints an error and returns. If any member has echo on, tx_mix, tx_volume, rx_volume, a pipeline in use, bf_enable, a negative pcm_id or a pcm_id different from the first member's, the conference falls back to software: every member gets CONF_SPLIT (if in an HFC conference) and PCM_DISC (if it has a slot) and its slots/banks and hfc_conf reset to -1, then conf->hardware = 0, conf->software = 1. With two otherwise eligible members it splits both from any HFC conference and either leaves already-crossed slot assignments in place or assigns new PCM slots (one shared slot with banks 0/1 when both have more than one PCM bank and different hfc_id, otherwise two crossed slots with bank 0) and sends PCM_CONN to both; if not enough free slots exist it falls back to software as above. With more than two members it falls back to software unless all are on the same HFC chip; if all members already have an HFC conference it just sets the flags; otherwise it joins every member to the existing HFC conference number or, if none, the lowest free unit 0..7 on that chip, giving each non-joined member a free PCM slot (banks 2, PCM_CONN) and sending MISDN_CTRL_HFC_CONF_JOIN; a member without features.hfc_conf or with hdlc set, no free slot or no free unit triggers the software fallback (members already moved may have been changed before the fallback resets them). On the hardware paths it sets conf->hardware = 1 and conf->software = tx_data, where tx_data is 1 if any member has dsp->tx_data.
note: slice cut the head: packet name dsp_cmx is invented; real function is dsp_cmx_hardware (file lines 364-1045). Old prose only described the outline. Read whole function including goto conf_software / one_member / join_members paths.

name: dsp_function
prose: Precondition: ch is the ch member embedded in a struct dsp and skb is a valid sk_buff whose mISDN header (mISDN_HEAD_P) carries the primitive. Postcondition: it dispatches on hh->prim; at the end, if a case left the switch with ret == 0 it frees skb with dev_kfree_skb and returns 0, while cases that return directly pass skb to a callee or queue it, and cases with a nonzero ret leave skb unfreed. PH_DATA_CNF: clears data_pending (without dsp_lock) and for hdlc schedules dsp->workq under dsp_lock if b_active; skb freed, 0. PH_DATA_IND/DL_DATA_IND: skb->len < 1 gives -EINVAL; for hdlc it calls dsp_cmx_hdlc under dsp_lock; otherwise under dsp_lock it decrypts if bf_enable, runs the rx pipeline if in use, changes rx volume if set, runs the software DTMF decoder if dtmf.software and calls dsp_cmx_receive if conf->software; outside the lock it then sends a PH_CONTROL_IND skb for each decoded digit to dsp->up (freeing that new skb on send failure or if up is NULL, skipping if allocation fails). Then if rx_disabled the skb is freed and 0 returned; else the prim becomes DL_DATA_IND and, when dsp->up is non-NULL, it returns the result of dsp->up->send(dsp->up, skb) (ownership passes to up), otherwise the skb is freed and 0 returned. PH_CONTROL_IND: id DTMF_HFC_COEF decodes coefficients without dsp_lock and sends a PH_CONTROL_IND per digit as above only when dtmf.hardware is set (ignored otherwise), skb freed, 0; id HFC_VOL_CHANGE_TX gives -EINVAL if skb->len != sizeof(int), else under dsp_lock sets tx_volume and calls dsp_cmx_hardware, dsp_dtmf_hardware and dsp_rx_off, skb freed, 0; any other id gives -EINVAL. PH_ACTIVATE_IND/CNF: under dsp_lock sets b_active = 1, data_pending = 0, rx_init = 1, rx_W = rx_R = 0, zeroes rx_buff and calls dsp_cmx_hardware, dsp_dtmf_hardware, dsp_rx_off; then prim = DL_ESTABLISH_CNF and it returns dsp->up->send(...) if up is non-NULL, else frees the skb and returns 0. PH_DEACTIVATE_IND/CNF: under dsp_lock sets b_active = 0, data_pending = 0, calls dsp_cmx_hardware and dsp_rx_off; prim = DL_RELEASE_CNF with the same forwarding. DL_DATA_REQ/PH_DATA_REQ: -EINVAL if skb->len < 1; for hdlc -EIO if !b_active, else it sets prim = PH_DATA_REQ, queues skb on dsp->sendq, schedules workq under dsp_lock and returns 0 without freeing; for non-hdlc it calls dsp_cmx_transmit under dsp_lock only when dsp->tone.tone is 0, then the skb is freed and 0 returned. PH_CONTROL_REQ: returns the result of dsp_control_req under dsp_lock (skb freed only if that is 0). DL_ESTABLISH_REQ/PH_ACTIVATE_REQ: without dsp_lock it runs dsp_dtmf_goertzel_init if dtmf hardware or software is on, get_features(ch) and dsp_fill_empty if features_fill_empty; prim = PH_ACTIVATE_REQ; returns ch->recv(ch->peer, skb) if ch->peer is non-NULL, else frees the skb and returns 0. DL_RELEASE_REQ/PH_DEACTIVATE_REQ: under dsp_lock it clears tone.tone/hardware/software, deletes the tone timer if pending, calls dsp_cmx_conf(dsp, 0) if dsp->conf and purges sendq; prim = PH_DEACTIVATE_REQ; returns ch->recv(ch->peer, skb) if peer non-NULL, else frees the skb and returns 0. Any other primitive returns -EINVAL with skb not freed.
note: reviewer R15 wrong: lines dsp_core.c:1581-1582 'if (!ret) dev_kfree_skb(skb)' frees skb on every case ending in break with ret 0 (PH_DATA_CNF, handled PH_CONTROL_IND). R1 (returns up->send result) right and R2 (lock coverage) right; both reflected. Prose rewritten to enumerate each case.

name: dsp_dtmf_goertzel_decode
prose: Precondition: dsp points to an initialized struct dsp whose dtmf state (buffer, size, count, lastwhat, lastdigit, treshold, digits[]) is valid; for fmt 0 (a-law) or 1 (u-law) data/len describe len sample bytes; for any other fmt (2 is used for HFC coefficients) data is read as 32-bit words in blocks of 64 bytes (16 words, 8 coefficient pairs). Postcondition: returns a pointer to dsp->dtmf.digits, a NUL-terminated string that is reset to empty on entry and then holds the digits newly detected in this call. For fmt 0/1 it converts samples through dsp_audio_law_to_s32 into the dtmf buffer until DSP_DTMF_NPOINTS samples are collected, saves the partial count in dsp->dtmf.size and returns when the data runs out before a full block; for a full block it computes the Goertzel energies. For other fmt, if len < 64 it logs an error when len > 0 and returns; otherwise it takes the 8 energies from the 64-byte block and consumes it. For each block it zeroes negative energies, takes the largest above dsp->dtmf.treshold, derives (lowgroup, highgroup), sets what to dtmf_matrix[low][high] if both groups are found and otherwise 0, sets dsp->dtmf.count to 0 when what differs from dsp->dtmf.lastwhat, and when count == 2 and what differs from dsp->dtmf.lastdigit it sets lastdigit = what and, if what is nonzero and strlen(digits)+1 < sizeof(digits), appends what to digits; when count != 2 it increments count; then it sets lastwhat = what and loops over the remaining data. No lock is taken.
note: slice cut the head: old prose called it void and described only the storedigit tail; real function (dsp_dtmf.c line 117) returns u8 * (dsp->dtmf.digits) and returns only from the two early-exit points (not enough samples, or HFC block shorter than 64 bytes). Also state is persisted across calls for fmt 0/1.

name: dsp_tone
prose: Precondition: dsp points to a valid struct dsp whose tone state (dsp->tone, including the timer tl) and features are initialized; tone is any int, 0 meaning stop the tone. Postcondition: it first clears tonet->software and tonet->hardware. If tone == 0 it deletes the tone timer if hfc_loops is set and the timer is pending, sends dsp_tone_hw_message(dsp, NULL, 0) when features.hfc_loops is set, sets tonet->tone = 0 and returns 0. Otherwise it searches the static pattern table for an entry whose tone equals the argument; if none is found it prints a KERN_WARNING and returns -EINVAL, leaving tonet->tone/pattern/index/count unchanged (software and hardware stay cleared). If found it sets tonet->tone, tonet->pattern = the entry, index = 0 and count = 0; with features.hfc_loops it sets tonet->hardware = 1, sends the first pattern data with dsp_tone_hw_message, deletes the timer if pending and arms tonet->tl for jiffies + pat->seq[0] * HZ / 8000; without hfc_loops it sets tonet->software = 1; in both cases it returns 0.
note: reviewer R15 wrong: tone 0 is explicitly handled (dsp_tones.c lines 1814-1820 of dump) and returns 0; only a non-zero tone not in the table gives -EINVAL. Clearing of software/hardware at entry is at the first two statements. slice cut the head: real function begins at file line 490.

name: sso_led_freq_set
prose: Precondition: priv->mmap is a valid regmap, pin is an LED pin number, freq_idx is a frequency rank in 0..10. Postcondition: returns void; no value is returned. If freq_idx == 0 it returns without writing. Otherwise it derives the pin's group (pins 0-23 group 0, 24-28 group 1, 29-31 group 2) and the clock source (rank 1-4 FPID, 5-8 GPTC, 9-10 GPTC_HS, any larger rank also GPTC_HS); for group 0 it returns without writing. For groups 1 and 2 the register is LED_BLINK_H8_0 (group 1) or LED_BLINK_H8_1 (group 2). Unless the source is GPTC_HS, it computes the rate value freq_idx-1 (FPID) or freq_idx-5 (GPTC) and calls regmap_update_bits with a three-bit mask GENMASK(low+2, low), low = off*6 + src*2 (off is the pin's offset within its group); the value passed is the rate shifted left by high (= low+2) rather than low, so only bit 0 of the rate can fall inside the mask (at the mask's top bit). It then calls regmap_update_bits for the clock-source field with mask GENMASK(low+2, low), low = GET_SRC_OFFSET(off), which the macro defines as pin*6+4 using the function's pin argument instead of off (for pins 24-31 this index lies beyond bit 31 of a 32-bit register), and value src << high, so source FPID writes 0, GPTC sets the mask's top bit and GPTC_HS writes 0 (its bit falls outside the mask). regmap_update_bits return values are ignored.
note: reviewers right: R1 (GPTC_HS ranks only update the source field, rate not written), R2 (rank 10 is GPTC_HS), R15 (GET_SRC_OFFSET(pinc) expands to ((pin)*6)+4 using pin not off at leds-lgm-sso.c:28, and values are shifted by high at lines 220-226). Old prose said the fields are set to the selected values: wrong.

name: apu_led_init
prose: Precondition: runs at module init (__init). Postcondition: if dmi_check_system(apu_led_dmi_table) finds no match it logs an error and returns -ENODEV without registering anything. Otherwise it calls platform_device_register_simple(KBUILD_MODNAME, -1, NULL, 0); if that returns an ERR_PTR it logs and returns the negative PTR_ERR with nothing registered. Otherwise it calls platform_driver_probe(&apu_led_driver, apu_led_probe); if that returns nonzero (for example a registration error, or -ENODEV when no device ended up bound to the driver, in which case platform_driver_probe unregisters the driver) it logs, unregisters the device with platform_device_unregister and returns that nonzero code. On success it returns 0 with the device registered and the driver registered and bound.
note: reviewers about contract only (contract dropped: touches global state; the 'result<0' form is vacuous). Prose checked against leds-apu.c:179-196 and platform.c __platform_driver_probe (returns -ENODEV and unregisters driver when nothing bound).

name: adb_request
prose: Precondition: req points to a valid adb_request whose data array can hold nbytes+1 bytes, the variadic arguments supply nbytes int values, and for ADBREQ_SYNC the caller should pass done == NULL (a non-NULL done only triggers WARN_ON and is then overwritten). Postcondition: returns -ENXIO without touching req if adb_controller or its send_request is NULL, and -EINVAL without touching req if nbytes < 1. Otherwise it sets req->nbytes = nbytes+1, req->done = done, req->reply_expected = flags & ADBREQ_REPLY, req->data[0] = ADB_PACKET and req->data[1..nbytes] to the variadic values. If ADBREQ_NOSEND is set it then returns 0 without sending and without touching req->arg. Otherwise, if ADBREQ_SYNC is set, it replaces req->done with adb_sync_req_done and points req->arg at an on-stack completion; it then calls adb_controller->send_request(req, 0) and returns its result rc, but when ADBREQ_SYNC is set, rc is 0 and req->complete is still clear it first blocks in wait_for_completion on that completion. After the call returns, req->arg (for the sync case) points to a dead stack object.
note: reviewer R15 right: NOSEND returns before the SYNC block (adb.c:1969-1975), so req->arg is never set on that path; R2 right: same. Old prose 'leaving req->done and req->arg exactly as just set' is wrong for arg. R1 right: SYNC overwrites req->done.

name: adbhid_input_keycode
prose: Precondition: adbhid[id] is a registered, non-NULL adbhid with a valid input device, flags and keycode table; scancode is any int; the repeat argument is unused. Postcondition: returns void. keycode = scancode & 0x7f and up_flag = scancode & 0x80. If restore_capslock_events is set: for keycode ADB_KEY_CAPSLOCK with up_flag clear, if FLAG_CAPSLOCK_IGNORE_NEXT is set it clears that flag and returns without reporting anything, otherwise it sets FLAG_CAPSLOCK_TRANSLATE | FLAG_CAPSLOCK_DOWN; else if scancode == 0xff (the whole value, not just low bits) and FLAG_POWER_KEY_PRESSED is clear, then if FLAG_CAPSLOCK_TRANSLATE is set it sets keycode = ADB_KEY_CAPSLOCK and either up_flag = 1 (clearing FLAG_CAPSLOCK_DOWN) when FLAG_CAPSLOCK_DOWN is set, or up_flag = 0 (clearing FLAG_CAPSLOCK_TRANSLATE) otherwise; if FLAG_CAPSLOCK_TRANSLATE is not set it logs 'Spurious caps lock event' and continues with keycode 0x7f. Then, if restore_capslock_events is clear and keycode is ADB_KEY_CAPSLOCK, it reports KEY_CAPSLOCK press then release (two input_report_key/input_sync pairs) and returns. Under CONFIG_PPC_PMAC only: ADB_KEY_POWER_OLD is remapped to ADB_KEY_POWER for PMAC_TYPE_COMET, HOOPER and KANGA; ADB_KEY_POWER updates FLAG_POWER_KEY_PRESSED and, if FLAG_FN_KEY_PRESSED is set or FLAG_POWER_FROM_FN is set, remaps to ADB_KEY_CMD and updates FLAG_POWER_FROM_FN; ADB_KEY_FN updates FLAG_FN_KEY_PRESSED and, on release with FLAG_EMU_FWDEL_DOWN set, clears that flag and remaps to ADB_KEY_FWDEL; ADB_KEY_DEL with FLAG_FN_KEY_PRESSED set remaps to ADB_KEY_FWDEL and updates FLAG_EMU_FWDEL_DOWN. Finally it looks up key = adbhid[id]->keycode[keycode]; if nonzero it reports input_report_key(key, !up_flag) followed by input_sync, else it logs an 'Unhandled ADB key' message. The function takes no lock.
note: reviewer R15 right: the 0xff test compares full scancode (adbhid.c:2017). R2 right (flag updates only in the listed cases); R1 right (early return and double CapsLock report). Old prose 'only low 7 bits and bit 7 used' was wrong for the 0xff check.

name: cuda_request
prose: Precondition: req is a valid writable adb_request with data space for nbytes bytes, and the variadic arguments supply nbytes ints. Postcondition: if the global via is NULL it sets req->complete = 1 and returns -ENXIO without queueing and without touching other fields. Otherwise it sets req->nbytes = nbytes and req->done = done, copies the nbytes variadic ints into req->data[0..nbytes-1] (stored as the data element type), sets req->reply_expected = 1 and returns cuda_write(req). cuda_write sets req->complete = 1 and returns -EINVAL if req->nbytes < 2 or req->data[0] > CUDA_PACKET; otherwise it clears next, sent, complete and reply_len, appends the request to the queue under cuda_lock (starting transmission via cuda_start when no request was in progress and the state is idle) and returns 0.
note: reviewer R15 wrong: cuda_request sets req->complete = 1 on the via == NULL path (via-cuda.c lines 2130-2133 of dump / file 480-484). Old prose right; added callee condition 'data[0] > CUDA_PACKET'. slice cut the head (real function begins at file line 478).

name: pmu_send_request
prose: Precondition: req points to a valid adb_request whose data[0] holds the packet type and whose nbytes gives the packet length; the caller keeps req alive until it completes. Postcondition: if pmu_state is uninitialized or !pmu_fully_inited it sets req->complete = 1 and returns -ENXIO. Otherwise ret starts at -EINVAL and it switches on data[0]. PMU_PACKET: shifts data down by one, decrements nbytes, sets reply[0] = ADB_RET_OK and reply_len = 1 when pmu_data_len[data[0]][1] is nonzero (else reply_len = 0, reply untouched) and ret = pmu_queue_request(req). CUDA_PACKET: only for data[1] == CUDA_GET_TIME with nbytes == 2 (rewritten to PMU_READ_RTC, nbytes 1, reply_len 3, reply[0..2] set) or data[1] == CUDA_SET_TIME with nbytes == 6 (rewritten to PMU_SET_RTC, nbytes 5, reply_len 3, reply[0..2] set) does it call pmu_queue_request; for any other data[1] or a wrong nbytes it leaves ret = -EINVAL. ADB_PACKET: if pmu_has_adb is false it returns -ENXIO immediately without touching req->complete; otherwise it rewrites data to a PMU_ADB_CMD packet (data[0] = PMU_ADB_CMD, data[2] = pmu_adb_flags, data[3] = nbytes-2, nbytes += 2), sets reply_expected = 1, reply_len = 0 and calls pmu_queue_request. Any other packet type leaves ret = -EINVAL. If ret is nonzero (including pmu_queue_request's -ENXIO or -EINVAL) it sets req->complete = 1 and returns ret. Otherwise, if sync is nonzero it calls pmu_poll until req->complete is set (pmu_queue_request can itself mark an empty request complete and return 0), and returns 0.
note: reviewer R15 right: unrecognized CUDA_PACKET data[1] gives -EINVAL (via-pmu.c:2176-2203 of dump); R1 right (ADB_PACKET !pmu_has_adb returns -ENXIO without complete); R2 right (reply[0] only set when pmu_data_len[..][1] != 0). Callee pmu_queue_request returns -ENXIO (uninit), -EINVAL (nbytes != expected), or 0 (also for nbytes <= 0 with complete=1).

name: cpu_check_overtemp
prose: Precondition: the module globals are initialized: cpu_thist holds CPU_TEMP_HIST_SIZE (180) samples, cpu_thist_pt is in [0,179], cpu_thist_total is their sum, cpu_all_tmax is set and failure_state holds the current failure bits; temp is a 16.16 fixed-point temperature. Postcondition: it computes new_state: FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP (8) if temp >= cpu_all_tmax + (10<<16) or the new average t_avg >= cpu_all_tmax + 0, and FAILURE_HIGH_OVERTEMP (16) if temp >= cpu_all_tmax + (14<<16) or t_avg >= cpu_all_tmax + (10<<16), printing messages for bits not already set in failure_state. It stores temp in cpu_thist[cpu_thist_pt], advances cpu_thist_pt modulo 180, updates cpu_thist_total and computes t_avg = total/180 (these history updates happen regardless of the outcome). If new_state is nonzero: if it contains FAILURE_HIGH_OVERTEMP it calls machine_power_off() (which normally does not return, but the code continues if it does); then, if new_state has any bit not already in failure_state, it calls cpu_max_all_fans(); it ORs new_state into failure_state. If new_state is zero, failure_state has FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP set and temp < cpu_all_tmax + ((-10)<<16), it prints a message and clears FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP. It returns failure_state & (FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP | FAILURE_HIGH_OVERTEMP), i.e. 0, 8, 16 or 24.
note: reviewers R2 and R15 right: machine_power_off() is not marked as no-return in this code path, execution continues (windfarm_pm112.c:2290-2294 of dump); fans condition is '(failure_state & new_state) != new_state' not 'low bit not already set'; return can be 16 or 24. Old prose said return was 0 or 8.

name: cpu_check_overtemp
prose: Precondition: temp is a signed 16.16 fixed-point CPU temperature; module globals cpu_all_tmax, cpu_thist, cpu_thist_pt, cpu_thist_total and failure_state are valid. Postcondition: it computes new_state, setting FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP (8) if temp >= cpu_all_tmax + (10<<16) or the average t_avg >= cpu_all_tmax, and FAILURE_HIGH_OVERTEMP (16) if temp >= cpu_all_tmax + (14<<16) or t_avg >= cpu_all_tmax + (10<<16), printing messages for bits not already in failure_state. On the first call only (static flag) it fills all CPU_TEMP_HIST_SIZE (180) history entries with temp and sets cpu_thist_total accordingly (after the immediate checks); on every call it then replaces cpu_thist[cpu_thist_pt] with temp, advances cpu_thist_pt modulo 180, updates cpu_thist_total and computes t_avg = total/180. If new_state is nonzero it calls machine_power_off() when it contains FAILURE_HIGH_OVERTEMP (execution continues if that call returns), calls cpu_max_all_fans() if new_state has a bit not already set in failure_state, and ORs new_state into failure_state. If new_state is zero, FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP is set in failure_state and temp < cpu_all_tmax + ((-10)<<16), it prints a message and clears FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP. It returns failure_state & (FAILURE_LOW_OVERTEMP | FAILURE_HIGH_OVERTEMP), i.e. 0, 8, 16 or 24.
note: reviewer R15 right: clearing LOW only happens when new_state == 0 (windfarm_pm72.c:2378-2389 of dump); R1 right (0x18 mask) ; R2 right. Old prose said 'normally does not return' without the continue case and clear without the new_state==0 qualification.

name: wf_smu_sys_fans_tick
prose: Precondition: st is a wf_smu_sys_fans_state initialized by wf_smu_create_sys_fans (valid pid, ticks, scale0/offset0/scale1/offset1, setpoints); sensor_hd_temp, fan_system, fan_hd, wf_smu_cpu_fans, wf_smu_failure_state and wf_smu_readjust are the module globals (fan_system, fan_hd and wf_smu_cpu_fans may be NULL; the function takes no lock). Postcondition: returns void. It decrements st->ticks; if the result is nonzero it returns when wf_smu_readjust is zero, or jumps to the fan-write step with the existing st->sys_setpoint and st->hd_setpoint when wf_smu_readjust is nonzero. If the result is zero it resets ticks to WF_SMU_SYS_FANS_INTERVAL and reads the HD temperature; on a sensor error it prints a warning, sets FAILURE_SENSOR in wf_smu_failure_state and returns without any fan call. Otherwise it sets FAILURE_OVERTEMP if temp > st->pid.param.itarget + 0x50000, runs wf_pid_run on temp, scales the result as (pid_out*scale0 >> 12) + offset0, computes cputarget as (wf_smu_cpu_fans ? its pid.target : 0), scaled by (cputarget*scale1 >> 12) + offset1 (so offset1 when wf_smu_cpu_fans is NULL), takes the larger of the two, raises it to at least st->pid.param.min and lowers it to at most st->pid.param.max. If the result equals st->sys_setpoint and the PID output equals st->hd_setpoint it returns with no fan call; otherwise it stores both and enters the fan-write step. That step calls wf_control_set(fan_system, st->sys_setpoint) only if fan_system is non-NULL and wf_smu_failure_state is zero, and then wf_control_set(fan_hd, st->hd_setpoint) only if fan_hd is non-NULL and wf_smu_failure_state is still zero; a wf_control_set error prints a warning and sets FAILURE_FAN, which also suppresses the second call. Any nonzero wf_smu_failure_state, including FAILURE_OVERTEMP set earlier in the same call, suppresses both writes.
note: reviewer R15 right: cputarget = 0 when wf_smu_cpu_fans is NULL is still scaled so result is offset1 (windfarm_pm81.c:2435-2436 of dump); R2 right (NULL checks, first failure skips second); R1 right. Old prose mostly right, one clause ambiguous.

name: wf_smu_cpu_fans_tick
prose: Precondition: st is a valid initialized wf_smu_cpu_fans_state (pid state, pid.param.tmax); sensor_cpu_temp and sensor_cpu_power are the module's sensor handles; fan_cpu_main, fan_cpu_second and fan_cpu_third are NULL or valid controls; the function takes no lock. Postcondition: returns void. It decrements st->ticks; if the result is nonzero it returns when wf_smu_readjust is false, or jumps to the fan-write step (skipping the tick reset, sensor reads and PID) when wf_smu_readjust is true. If the result is zero it resets ticks to WF_SMU_CPU_FANS_INTERVAL and reads the CPU temperature and then the CPU power sensor; an error from either prints a warning, sets FAILURE_SENSOR in wf_smu_failure_state and returns without fan writes. Otherwise it sets FAILURE_OVERTEMP when temp > st->pid.param.tmax (or > 0x4a0000 if HACKED_OVERTEMP is defined), and still runs wf_cpu_pid_run(&st->pid, power, temp). If the new setpoint equals st->cpu_setpoint it returns without fan writes; otherwise it stores it and enters the fan-write step. That step calls wf_control_set(fan_cpu_main, st->cpu_setpoint), then fan_cpu_second, then fan_cpu_third, each only if non-NULL and only while wf_smu_failure_state is zero; a wf_control_set error prints a warning and sets FAILURE_FAN, which suppresses the remaining fan writes in that call, as does any nonzero wf_smu_failure_state, including FAILURE_OVERTEMP set earlier in the call (a changed setpoint is still stored in st->cpu_setpoint).
note: reviewers: R1 right (PID still advanced after overtemp), R2 right (readjust path skips tick reset/sensors), R15 wrong: the code does not set fans to max on failure_state and later fans are NOT written after a set error because each call re-tests wf_smu_failure_state == 0 (windfarm_pm91.c:2519-2536 of dump). Prose kept, small additions.

name: flexrm_mbox_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is the platform device of a Broadcom FlexRM mailbox with a register resource at index 0 and platform MSI support. Postcondition: returns 0 after allocating (devm) the mbox and ring structures, mapping the registers, counting and initializing the rings, setting a DMA mask, creating the BD and completion DMA pools, allocating one platform MSI per ring, optionally creating debugfs entries when debugfs is initialized, and registering the mailbox controller (devm), then logging the channel count. The DMA mask step tries dma_set_mask_and_coherent(40 bits) and, if that fails, 32 bits; the probe fails only if both fail, returning that error. Error returns: -ENOMEM if the mbox or ring allocation, the DMA pool creation or the controller chans allocation fails; -ENODEV if the memory resource is missing or smaller than RING_REGS_SIZE, no ring with RING_VER_MAGIC is found, or the init scan runs out of rings; PTR_ERR of the register mapping if the resource check passed but mapping failed; the error from platform_device_msi_init_and_alloc_irqs; the error from devm_mbox_controller_register. Cleanup on failure: a failure creating the completion pool destroys the BD pool; a failure in MSI allocation destroys both pools; a failure after MSI allocation (chans allocation or controller registration) also removes the debugfs root recursively and frees the platform MSIs before destroying both pools. Earlier failures need no explicit cleanup; devm resources are released by the driver core.
note: slice cut the head: packet name flexrm_mbox_probe_dma_mask_fallback is an invented fragment label (not a function); real enclosing function is flexrm_mbox_probe (file lines 1475-1641), slice starts at 1555. Fixed under the real name rather than dropped.

name: STORE(bch_cached_dev)
prose: Generated function bch_cached_dev_store(kobj, attr, buf, size) from STORE(bch_cached_dev). Precondition: kobj is the disk.kobj of a registered cached_dev, buf holds the user's written text of length size, and the caller does not hold bch_register_lock (it is taken here). Postcondition: if bcache_is_reboot is set it returns -EBUSY without taking the lock. Otherwise it takes bch_register_lock and calls __cached_dev_store, whose return value (the byte count or a negative errno) becomes the result. If attr is sysfs_writeback_running: when dc->writeback_thread is NULL or an error pointer, and dc->writeback_running is true after the inner call, it resets writeback_running to false and logs an error; if the thread exists it calls bch_writeback_queue(dc). If attr is sysfs_writeback_percent, and dc->disk.c is non-NULL and BCACHE_DEV_WB_RUNNING was not already set (test_and_set_bit), it schedules writeback_rate_update after writeback_rate_update_seconds * HZ jiffies. These follow-up actions run regardless of whether the inner call succeeded. It releases bch_register_lock and returns the inner call's value.
note: reviewer R15 right: the error log is printed only when dc->writeback_running is true after the inner store (sysfs.c STORE(bch_cached_dev)); old prose said it logged whenever no thread exists. Name set to macro head STORE(bch_cached_dev); the real function is bch_cached_dev_store.

name: STRTO_H(strtoint, int)
prose:
Generated function bch_strtoint_h(cp, res) from STRTO_H(strtoint, int). Precondition: cp points to a NUL-terminated string and res to writable int storage. Postcondition: it parses a number with simple_strtol(cp, &e, 10) (assigned to a int, so for the int/unsigned int variants the long result is converted to 32 bits) and then examines the character *e, case-insensitively: a suffix k, m, g, t, p, e, z or y multiplies the value by 1024 once for k, twice for m, three times for g, four for t, five for p, six for e, and seven times for each of z and y (the same count); a suffix with e equal to cp (no digits parsed) returns -EINVAL; '
' or '\0' means no suffix; any other character returns -EINVAL. After the suffix, at most one '

name: q_requeue
prose: Precondition: q is initialized with q->nr_levels > 0; e is an entry currently linked in q at its level e->level < q->nr_levels with pending_work false; any entry that may be displaced also has pending_work false (q_push and q_push_before BUG_ON otherwise); if s1 is non-NULL it is linked at e's old level, and s2 must be non-NULL and in that level when exactly one sentinel is passed. Postcondition: returns void. new_level = min(q->nr_levels - 1, e->level + extra_levels). If extra_levels is nonzero and e->level < q->nr_levels - 1, it scans level new_level from its head past sentinel entries, counting them in sentinels_passed; if a non-sentinel entry de is found, de is removed from that level, its level set to e's old level, and reinserted there: if s1 is non-NULL it is inserted before s1 when no sentinel was passed, before s2 when exactly one was passed, and at the tail otherwise; if s1 is NULL it is inserted at the tail. If no such de exists, nothing is displaced. Finally e is removed from its old level, its level set to new_level and it is pushed at the tail of that level. q->nr_elts is unchanged because each removed non-sentinel entry is pushed back once.
note: reviewers: R1 right (displacement only if de exists), R2 right (only pending_work BUG_ONs; s1/s2 must belong to e's old level) -- prose already reflects both; kept. Source dm-cache-policy-smq.c:472-506.
